title: The Acts of the Apostles Timeline
sub: Jerusalem · Judea and Samaria · the End of the Earth · Every Chapter, Chapter & Verse
desc: Luke's own sequel to his Gospel, tracing the church from a locked room in Jerusalem to Paul preaching unhindered in Rome — structured around the book's own thesis (Acts 1:8) and its six recurring growth summaries, with the ministry pivoting from Peter to Paul at its center.

eras.label: Era One · Acts 1:1-2:47
eras.name: The Church Is Born
eras.dates: An ascension, a replacement apostle, and the Spirit falling on a crowd of pilgrims

events.title: The Ascension; 'Witnesses to the End of the Earth'
events.detail: Luke's own sequel opens by naming its first volume, then gives the whole book's structural thesis in one line — Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria, and the end of the earth — before Jesus is lifted into a cloud and two angels promise His return 'in just the same way.'

events.title: Matthias Chosen to Replace Judas
events.detail: Back in the upper room, 120 believers wait in prayer; Peter reads Judas's betrayal and death as fulfilled prophecy, and the eleven cast lots between two candidates to restore the number to twelve before Pentecost.

events.title: Pentecost: The Spirit Falls; Speaking in Tongues
events.detail: A sound like a violent wind, tongues like fire, and suddenly a room full of Galileans is understood by pilgrims from over a dozen nations, each hearing 'the mighty deeds of God' in their own language — while others in the crowd simply mock them as drunk.

events.title: Peter's Sermon; Three Thousand Baptized
events.detail: Peter's first sermon reframes the scene through Joel's prophecy and Psalm 16, lands on the claim that God has made 'this Jesus whom you crucified' both Lord and Christ, and the crowd is 'pierced to the heart' — about three thousand are baptized that day.

events.title: The First Church: Devoted, Sharing, Growing
events.detail: A snapshot of the earliest community — apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, prayer, and everything held in common — closing on the first of Acts' recurring growth summaries: 'the Lord was adding to their number daily.'

eras.label: Era Two · Acts 3:1-5:42
eras.name: Signs, Growth, and the First Pushback
eras.dates: A lame man healed at the temple gate draws both a crowd and the Sanhedrin

events.title: A Lame Man Healed at the Beautiful Gate
events.detail: Peter has 'no silver and gold' but heals a man lame from birth in Jesus' name — he goes into the temple 'walking and leaping and praising God,' and the astonished crowd recognizes him as the beggar who used to sit there.

events.title: Peter's Second Sermon: 'The Author of Life'
events.detail: Peter refuses credit for the healing and preaches again — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has glorified Jesus, whom the crowd 'put to death the Author of life,' but repentance now can bring 'times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord.'

events.title: Peter and John Before the Sanhedrin
events.detail: Arrested overnight for proclaiming the resurrection, Peter and John face the same council that condemned Jesus and declare 'there is salvation in no one else' — the rulers, unable to deny an undeniable healed man standing right there, can only warn them to stop and let them go.

events.title: The Church Prays; the Place Is Shaken
events.detail: Released, Peter and John report back and the whole church prays together, quoting Psalm 2 against the rulers who opposed 'His Christ' — the place shakes, and they are filled with the Spirit and speak with boldness.

events.title: One Heart and Soul; Barnabas Introduced
events.detail: The believers hold everything in common again, with 'great grace... upon them all' — Joseph, nicknamed Barnabas ('son of encouragement') by the apostles, is introduced here selling a field and giving the proceeds, a generosity about to be counterfeited.

events.title: Ananias and Sapphira
events.detail: A married couple sell property, secretly keep back part of the price, and lie to the Holy Spirit about it — both fall down dead on the spot when confronted, and 'great fear came over the whole church.'

events.title: Signs and Wonders; Peter's Shadow
events.detail: The apostles' reputation grows so far that the sick are carried into the streets hoping 'at least his shadow might fall on' Peter — crowds from surrounding towns bring the sick and demon-afflicted, and 'they were all being healed.'

events.title: Arrested Again; Gamaliel's Counsel; 'We Must Obey God'
events.detail: Jailed by the jealous high priest and Sadducees, the apostles are freed overnight by an angel and found right back in the temple teaching by morning; Peter answers the council's fury with 'we must obey God rather than men,' and only the Pharisee Gamaliel's counsel — wait and see if it's from God — spares them, though they're flogged first and 'rejoicing that they had been considered worthy to suffer shame for the Name.'

eras.label: Era Three · Acts 6:1-8:3
eras.name: Stephen: The First Martyr
eras.dates: A dispute over widows produces seven deacons — and one who is stoned to death

events.title: Seven Chosen to Serve; the Word Keeps Spreading
events.detail: Greek-speaking widows are being overlooked in the daily food distribution; the apostles hand off practical ministry to seven Spirit-filled men — including Stephen and Philip — so they can focus on prayer and teaching, and the growth summary lands again: 'a great many of the priests were becoming obedient to the faith.'

events.title: Stephen Seized; False Witnesses
events.detail: Full of grace and power, Stephen debates members of a Hellenistic synagogue who cannot out-argue him — so they recruit false witnesses to accuse him of blasphemy against Moses and the temple, and his face is seen 'like the face of an angel' as he stands before the council.

events.title: Stephen's Speech: Israel's History Retold
events.detail: The longest single speech in Acts sweeps from Abraham through Joseph, Moses, and the wilderness tabernacle to Solomon's temple, arguing Israel has always resisted God's messengers and 'the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands' — closing with the sharpest line yet: 'you always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.'

events.title: Stephen Stoned; Saul Approves; Persecution Scatters the Church
events.detail: Enraged, the council drags Stephen out and stones him while he prays 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' — a young man named Saul watches the coats and approves of the killing, then begins ravaging the church house by house, scattering believers throughout Judea and Samaria exactly as Acts 1:8 foretold.

eras.label: Era Four · Acts 8:4-9:31
eras.name: Judea, Samaria, and Saul's Turn
eras.dates: The gospel crosses into Samaria, reaches an Ethiopian official, and stops a persecutor cold

events.title: Philip in Samaria; Simon the Magician
events.detail: Scattered believers preach wherever they go; Philip's Samaritan crusade draws crowds and even converts a famous sorcerer, Simon — who then tries to buy the Spirit's power with money and gets Peter's sharpest rebuke: 'may your silver perish with you.'

events.title: Philip and the Ethiopian Eunuch
events.detail: An angel sends Philip to a desert road where he finds a high court official of Ethiopia's queen reading Isaiah's suffering-servant poem aloud — Philip explains it's about Jesus, baptizes him on the spot, and is instantly 'snatched away' by the Spirit.

events.title: Saul's Conversion on the Damascus Road
events.detail: Still 'breathing threats and murder,' Saul is blinded by a light from heaven and hears Jesus Himself ask why he is being persecuted — three days blind and fasting, he's healed and baptized by a reluctant disciple named Ananias, told this former persecutor is now 'a chosen instrument... to bear My name before the Gentiles and kings.'

events.title: Saul Preaches in Damascus; Escapes in a Basket
events.detail: The former persecutor immediately starts proclaiming Jesus in the synagogues, baffling everyone who knew him — a murder plot forces him over the city wall in a basket by night, and even in Jerusalem the disciples are afraid of him until Barnabas vouches for his story.

eras.label: Era Five · Acts 9:32-12:25
eras.name: Peter, Cornelius, and the Door to the Gentiles
eras.dates: A vision of unclean animals breaks open the gospel to a Roman centurion's household

events.title: Peter Heals Aeneas; Raises Tabitha (Dorcas)
events.detail: On a ministry circuit, Peter heals a paralyzed man at Lydda and, at Joppa, raises a beloved disciple named Tabitha from the dead — word spreads and 'many believed in the Lord,' setting the stage for the vision that follows.

events.title: Cornelius's Vision; Peter's Rooftop Vision
events.detail: A devout Roman centurion is told by an angel to send for Peter; simultaneously Peter, praying on a rooftop, sees a sheet of unclean animals lowered from heaven three times with the command 'what God has cleansed, no longer consider defiled' — the two visions converge as Cornelius's messengers arrive at Peter's door.

events.title: 'God Shows No Partiality'; the Spirit Falls on Gentiles
events.detail: Peter preaches in a Gentile home for the first time, opening with the line that reframes the whole book — 'God is not one to show partiality' — and the Holy Spirit falls on Cornelius's household mid-sermon, astonishing the Jewish believers who came with him, before they're baptized.

events.title: Peter Defends Himself in Jerusalem
events.detail: Circumcised believers in Jerusalem confront Peter for eating with uncircumcised Gentiles; he retells the whole vision and Spirit-outpouring in order, and the objection dissolves into praise: 'God has granted to the Gentiles also the repentance that leads to life.'

events.title: The Church at Antioch; 'Christians' First Named
events.detail: Believers scattered by Stephen's persecution start preaching to Greeks at Antioch, and a large number believe; Barnabas fetches Saul from Tarsus to help teach there for a full year — it's in Antioch, not Jerusalem, that the disciples are first called Christians, and the church sends relief aid back to Judea for a coming famine.

events.title: Herod Kills James, Imprisons Peter; an Angel Frees Him
events.detail: Herod Agrippa has the apostle James executed and, seeing it please the crowd, arrests Peter too — an angel walks him past sleeping guards and a self-opening gate in the night, and Herod, later accepting worship as a god instead of giving God the glory, is struck down and 'eaten by worms.' The chapter closes with the growth summary again: 'the word of the Lord continued to grow and to be multiplied.'

eras.label: Era Six · Acts 13:1-15:35
eras.name: The First Missionary Journey and the Jerusalem Council
eras.dates: Paul and Barnabas are formally sent out, and the church has to decide what a Gentile convert owes the Law

events.title: Barnabas and Saul Set Apart; a Sorcerer Struck Blind
events.detail: The Holy Spirit tells the Antioch church to release Barnabas and Saul for the work; on Cyprus, a Jewish sorcerer trying to turn a Roman proconsul away from the faith is struck blind by Saul — who from this point on goes by his Roman name, Paul.

events.title: Paul's Synagogue Sermon at Pisidian Antioch; 'We Turn to the Gentiles'
events.detail: Paul's first recorded sermon sweeps Israel's history to David to Jesus' death and resurrection exactly as Peter's did, but ends differently: rejected by the synagogue, Paul and Barnabas declare 'we are turning to the Gentiles,' and 'the word of the Lord was being spread through the whole region.'

events.title: Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe; Mistaken for Gods
events.detail: A healed lame man at Lystra convinces the crowd that Paul and Barnabas are Zeus and Hermes come down as men — they tear their clothes refusing the sacrifice, and days later the same city that wanted to worship Paul stones him and leaves him for dead; he gets up and keeps going, and the pair return to Antioch to report 'how He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.'

events.title: The Jerusalem Council: Must Gentiles Be Circumcised?
events.detail: A real crisis — some teach Gentile converts must be circumcised to be saved — brings Paul and Barnabas to Jerusalem, where Peter, then James, argue from experience and prophecy that God has already accepted the Gentiles by faith alone; the council's letter lays only a few minimal requirements on Gentile believers, a decision James Heiser and others read as the hinge of the whole book.

eras.label: Era Seven · Acts 15:36-18:22
eras.name: The Second Missionary Journey
eras.dates: A sharp split sends Paul west with Silas instead, all the way to Corinth

events.title: Paul and Barnabas Split; Timothy Joins
events.detail: A sharp disagreement over whether to bring John Mark again splits the partnership — Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus, Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia, picking up young Timothy at Lystra along the way and having him circumcised for the sake of the Jewish communities they'll enter.

events.title: The Macedonian Call; Lydia Converted at Philippi
events.detail: Forbidden by the Spirit from preaching in Asia and Bithynia, Paul sees a vision of a Macedonian man begging 'come over... and help us' — crossing into Europe for the first time, the first convert is Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth, whose household is baptized at a riverside prayer meeting.

events.title: A Slave Girl Freed; Paul and Silas Jailed; an Earthquake
events.detail: Paul casts a spirit of fortune-telling out of an enslaved girl, costing her owners their profit; beaten and jailed, Paul and Silas sing hymns at midnight until an earthquake springs every door — the terrified jailer, about to kill himself, instead asks 'what must I do to be saved?' and is baptized with his whole household before dawn.

events.title: Thessalonica and Berea; 'Examining the Scriptures Daily'
events.detail: Run out of Thessalonica by a jealous mob, Paul finds the Bereans 'more noble-minded' — they check everything he says against Scripture themselves before believing, a model of verification the text holds up approvingly.

events.title: Paul at the Areopagus: 'To an Unknown God'
events.detail: In Athens, provoked by a city full of idols, Paul builds his sermon to the philosophers from an altar 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD' and even quotes their own poets — mention of resurrection splits the crowd between sneering and curiosity, and only a few, including Dionysius the Areopagite, believe.

events.title: Corinth: Aquila, Priscilla, and Gallio's Dismissal
events.detail: Paul settles a year and a half in Corinth with fellow tentmakers Aquila and Priscilla; when Jewish leaders drag him before the proconsul Gallio, he refuses to even hear the case, calling it a dispute over 'words and names and your own law' — not a Roman crime.

eras.label: Era Eight · Acts 18:23-21:16
eras.name: The Third Missionary Journey
eras.dates: Two years in Ephesus, a riot over a goddess, and the road back to Jerusalem despite every warning

events.title: Apollos Corrected; Disciples Re-Baptized at Ephesus
events.detail: Apollos, eloquent but only knowing John's baptism, is quietly corrected by Priscilla and Aquila; Paul finds a dozen Ephesian disciples in the same position and lays hands on them — they receive the Holy Spirit and speak in tongues for the first time.

events.title: Ephesus: Handkerchiefs, Failed Exorcists, Burned Scrolls
events.detail: Extraordinary miracles happen through Paul — even cloths that touched him heal the sick — while seven sons of a Jewish priest trying to copy his exorcism formula get overpowered and stripped by the possessed man; awestruck new believers publicly burn a fortune in magic scrolls.

events.title: The Silversmiths' Riot: 'Great Is Artemis!'
events.detail: A silversmith named Demetrius, seeing his idol-shrine trade threatened by Paul's preaching, incites a two-hour chant in the theater until the city clerk finally calms the mob by pointing out there's no actual legal charge to bring.

events.title: Farewell Tour; Eutychus Falls Asleep and Dies
events.detail: Retracing his steps through Macedonia and Greece, Paul preaches so long past midnight at Troas that a young man named Eutychus falls asleep on a windowsill, drops three stories, and is picked up dead — Paul embraces him and he's found alive, and the meeting resumes until dawn.

events.title: Paul's Farewell to the Ephesian Elders
events.detail: Summoned to Miletus, Paul gives the only speech in Acts addressed purely to a Christian audience — warning of 'savage wolves' to come, insisting he's 'innocent of the blood of all,' and quoting a saying of Jesus found nowhere in the Gospels: 'it is more blessed to give than to receive.' They weep, certain they'll never see his face again.

events.title: Agabus's Warning; 'The Will of the Lord Be Done'
events.detail: Sailing toward Jerusalem despite repeated Spirit-prompted warnings, Paul is met at Caesarea by the prophet Agabus, who binds his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to predict exactly what will happen — Paul refuses to be talked out of it: 'I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.'

eras.label: Era Nine · Acts 21:17-23:35
eras.name: Arrest in Jerusalem
eras.dates: A temple riot, a rescue by Roman soldiers, and two very different audiences for one defense speech

events.title: Paul Seized in the Temple; Rescued by Roman Troops
events.detail: To calm rumors that he teaches Jews to abandon Moses, Paul joins four men in a purification rite at the temple — but Jews from Asia spot him, falsely claim he defiled the temple with a Gentile, and a mob drags him out to kill him until a Roman commander and his troops physically pull him free.

events.title: Paul's Defense Speech to the Jerusalem Crowd
events.detail: Speaking Hebrew from the barracks steps, Paul quiets the crowd by retelling his conversion in full — the same Damascus road story Luke already told once in chapter 9, now in Paul's own first-person voice — until the word 'Gentiles' sets them shouting again.

events.title: 'I Was Born a Roman Citizen'
events.detail: About to be flogged for information, Paul reveals his Roman citizenship just in time — illegal to bind, let alone beat, a Roman without trial — and the commander who paid for his own citizenship is suddenly afraid of what he's already done.

events.title: Before the Sanhedrin; Pharisees vs. Sadducees; a Night Vision
events.detail: Paul splits the council by declaring he's on trial over the resurrection, setting Pharisees and Sadducees against each other so violently the Romans have to physically remove him again — that night the Lord appears: 'as you have testified at Jerusalem, so you must testify at Rome also.'

events.title: A Forty-Man Assassination Plot; Smuggled to Caesarea
events.detail: More than forty men vow to fast until Paul is dead; his nephew overhears the plot and reports it, and the commander responds by night-marching Paul to Caesarea under a 470-soldier guard, handing him off to the governor Felix with a letter clearing him of any capital charge.

eras.label: Era Ten · Acts 24:1-26:32
eras.name: Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
eras.dates: Two years of Roman custody and three hearings, none of which find any real charge

events.title: Before Felix; 'Go Away for the Present'
events.detail: A hired orator accuses Paul of being a plague and a Nazarene ringleader; Paul calmly rebuts every charge and preaches 'righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come' until Felix, frightened, cuts him off — he leaves Paul in custody two full years, partly hoping for a bribe.

events.title: Before Festus; 'I Appeal to Caesar'
events.detail: Felix's successor Festus is ready to send Paul back to Jerusalem for trial — straight into the still-active assassination plot — so Paul exercises his citizen's right and appeals directly to Caesar, ending any further local jurisdiction over his case.

events.title: Festus Briefs King Agrippa
events.detail: With Paul already appealed to Rome, Festus admits to King Agrippa he has 'nothing definite... to write to my lord' — the charges amount to a dead man Paul claims is alive — and asks Agrippa to help him find something worth writing down.

events.title: Paul's Defense Before Agrippa: 'Almost Persuadest Me'
events.detail: Paul's most polished defense speech retells his conversion a third time, aimed squarely at a king who knows Jewish custom — Festus interrupts calling him mad, but Agrippa's own verdict, given privately afterward, is that Paul 'could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.'

eras.label: Era Eleven · Acts 27:1-28:31
eras.name: Storm, Shipwreck, and Rome
eras.dates: A fourteen-day storm, a viper that doesn't kill him, and an ending that refuses to end

events.title: The Storm and Shipwreck at Malta
events.detail: Ignoring Paul's warning not to sail, the ship is caught in a violent Euraquilo gale for fourteen days — cargo jettisoned, all hope abandoned — until an angel promises Paul 'God has granted you all those who are sailing with you'; the ship finally breaks apart on a reef, and all 276 aboard reach Malta alive exactly as promised.

events.title: A Viper's Bite; Healing on Malta
events.detail: Bitten by a viper while gathering firewood, Paul shakes it off unharmed — the islanders flip from calling him a murderer to calling him a god — and he heals the sick of the island, including the father of the leading official, over their three-month winter stay.

events.title: Arrival in Rome
events.detail: The final leg by ship brings Paul to Puteoli, then overland to Rome itself, where believers walk out as far as the Market of Appius to meet him — seeing them, Paul 'thanked God and took courage.'

events.title: Two Years Under Guard, Preaching Unhindered
events.detail: Paul's own account to Rome's Jewish leaders draws a mixed response, and he closes with Isaiah's old warning about ears that won't hear; the book itself ends without resolution to Paul's case — two full years under house arrest, 'preaching the kingdom of God... with all confidence, unhindered,' a deliberately open ending rather than a tidy one.
